stem: A single canopy sensor suddenly differs from two colocated verified sensors after maintenance. What should happen before changing room controls?
choices: Verify the suspect sensor's placement, physical condition, recent maintenance effects, and calibration/data quality before changing room controls.
Adjust the room controls toward the outlier value because a recently serviced sensor may be more accurate than older colocated sensors.
Use the average of all three sensors as the control value while continuing to watch for a persistent difference.
Temporarily exclude the two matching sensors from the comparison because agreement between them could reflect a shared calibration bias.
rationale: A sudden disagreement that appears immediately after maintenance raises a data-quality question before it raises a control question. The outlier may reflect placement, damage, configuration, contamination, calibration drift, or a maintenance-related change. Verifying the suspect sensor against known-good or colocated references protects the room from an unnecessary high-consequence control adjustment. Averaging the readings can hide a faulty input, and acting on the outlier assumes accuracy before the measurement system has been checked.
